findings.issue: Wave 2 co-edits: Task 3 and Task 4 both modify news_bot.py AND tests/test_integration.py in the same wave. This is not a shared-resource competition (Task 3 owns the REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED flag + E014 send-site region ~L130/~L2374; Task 4 owns the new resolve_dedup_callback near ~L469; both add disjoint new test classes TestDedupReviewButtons vs TestResolveDedupCallback). Edits are purely additive and region-disjoint, so correctness is intact, but a parallel executor must merge the two news_bot.py / test_integration.py edits without clobbering. Informational heads-up, not a task defect.
findings.fix: When running Wave 2 in parallel, apply Task 3 and Task 4 edits to news_bot.py and tests/test_integration.py additively (distinct functions + distinct test classes); no content change required.

shared_resource_ownership.detail: Review-token store (put/get/delete_review_token) + PRAGMA busy_timeout: sole owner Task 1; consumers Task 3 (put) and Task 4 (get/delete) both declare depends_on Task 1. REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED flag: sole owner Task 3 (explicitly states 'единственное определение константы', instructs reuse-not-duplicate); consumer Task 5 reads news_bot.REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED as a module attribute and declares depends_on Task 3; Task 6 (docs) also depends on Task 3. No competing/second definition. resolve_dedup_callback: sole owner Task 4; consumer Task 5 depends on Task 4.

contract_consistency.detail: action arg: Task 4 branches strictly on full words action=='cancel'/'keep' (with an explicit note calling out Task 5); Task 5 maps c->'cancel', k->'keep' before calling resolve_dedup_callback (with matching explicit note). callback_data grammar: Task 2 builder emits 'dd:c:<token>' (cancel) then 'dd:k:<token>' (keep); Task 3 integration test asserts ['dd:c:<token>','dd:k:<token>']; Task 5 parser reads 'dd:<c|k>:<token>'. Order (cancel first, keep second) consistent across builder, send-site test, and parser. Token scheme secrets.token_urlsafe(9) consistent (import secrets added by owning Task 3). Status strings and 'review listener active' startup log consistent across Tasks 4/5/6/11/12.

no_competing_instances_same_wave.detail: No two same-wave tasks each create their own instance of a heavy/shared resource. Wave 1: Task 1 (repo) vs Task 2 (admin_alerts + send_admin_notification) - disjoint. Wave 2: Task 3 (flag/send-site) vs Task 4 (resolve logic) - disjoint owners, only additive co-editing of news_bot.py (see minor finding). Wave 3: Task 5 (listener code) vs Task 6 (docs only) - disjoint files. Wave 4: Tasks 7/8/9 all analysis-only, no code mutation.
